A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PanoLlama work. All 25 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison. The former application-details Appendix D is retained as Appendix E in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original panorama-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1 and A1, ablations in Figures 4–6, and qualitative results throughout the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original quantitative comparisons, ablations, application demonstrations, and appendix qualitative results.

M1.justification: Token redirection, horizontal and vertical expansion, decoding, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Specifying Llama XL and acknowledging partial-context conditioning provide additional documentation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same text-to-panorama coverage across 25 main themes, 100+ sub-themes, and photorealistic and artistic styles, with the same application scenarios. New Appendix D describes existing dataset construction rather than demonstrating added coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain BLD, MD, TD, SyncD, MAD, and SMD. Appendix C retains the same four SDXL comparators: BLDXL, MDXL, TDXL, and MADXL. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated resolutions, expansion strides, metrics, cropping procedures, and timing protocol remain unchanged. However, new Appendix D reports 400 prompts per theme across 25 themes, while Section 4.1 retains 1,000 prompts overall. Without an explanation of selection or sampling, a changed sample pool cannot be distinguished from a documentation error.

E4.justification: The expansion-stride, panorama-size, and prompt-theme analyses retain identical figures and settings. The blending analysis is also retained in the renamed application appendix. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 25 sets of random seeds and mean metric scores. Neither introduces new run-count disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and A1, plotted results, and qualitative images are unchanged. The qualitative summaries are slightly narrowed: Section 4.1 drops the missing-key-features criticism of MAD, and Section 4.2 removes animal from the examples of weaker prompt themes.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 removes the explicit joint-diffusion negative log-likelihood objective given as Equation 13 in v2. The neighboring-crop factorization in Equation 12 and PanoLlama's mathematical formulation remain. The appendix blending equation is merely renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract, four principal contributions, headline performance claims, and conclusion retain the same scientific scope. Explicitly describing planar panoramas clarifies the existing task framing rather than introducing a different contribution.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the limitation about weak focal points and subject layout with an acknowledgment that finite token capacity permits only approximate global conditioning. New Appendix D also argues that randomized, diverse prompt construction ensures fairness. Most result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix D documents scene-scale theme selection, 3–8 sub-themes per theme, randomized styles, and AI-generated prompts, although its prompt count is unreconciled. Appendix A specifies Llama XL instead of simply Llama. Existing pseudocode, hardware information, blending parameters, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Text2Light, DynamicID, and WonderFree and clarifies its planar-panorama positioning relative to spherical panorama work. The broader related-work organization and claimed distinction from diffusion methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized grammar corrections and paragraph refinements accompany the rewritten limitations, new dataset-construction appendix, and acknowledgements. The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 6 shift within page 7, and text and appendix material reflow around the edits. Figure images, axes, legends, table structures, and all thirteen appendix comparison figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency about finite-context conditioning and adds useful generator and dataset-construction details. However, its new 400-prompts-per-theme statement conflicts with the retained 1,000-prompt dataset description, and it removes the earlier subject-layout limitation. Section 3.3 also retains the claim of conditioning on all preceding crops despite the new qualification. These benefits and unresolved inconsistencies prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality.
